why: The minimum cost to reach a target: the frog reaches stone i only from i-1 or i-2, so best[i] = min(best[i-1] + |h[i]-h[i-1]|, best[i-2] + |h[i]-h[i-2]|). It is climbing stairs with min instead of +.
hints: How could the frog have arrived at stone i? There are only two possible previous stones.
best[0] = 0; best[i] = min over the two predecessors j of best[j] + abs(heights[i] - heights[j]). Write it recursively with memo first, then as a loop.
Keep the last two values only. O(n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: A greedy 'take the cheaper next jump' fails; the DP must compare both full paths.
Heights can be negative; abs handles that.
